chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ibn Mahboub, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

The believer does not cease to be in goodness and hope for the mercy of Allah, Exalted and Majestic, as long as he does not hasten, so he despairs and leaves supplication. I said to him, 'How does he hasten?' He said, 'He says, I have been supplicating since such and such (time) and I do not see the answer.'

key_terms.يَسْتَعْجِلُ: To hasten or be impatient for the response

ai.seo_question: What does it mean to 'hasten' in supplication according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Shaykh al-Kulayni records this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) to clarify that 'hastening' (istijlal) is not merely waiting, but a spiritual failure characterized by despair and the cessation of dua. This hadith serves as a practical guide for believers to maintain persistent supplication during periods of divine delay, emphasizing that the state of hope itself is a mercy that preserves the believer's goodness until the appointed time.
